In this paper we address these problems by proposing a novel
taxonomy of fixation identification algorithms and evaluating
representative algorithms in the context of this taxonomy.
The taxonomy classifies algorithms with respect to five spatial
and temporal criteria. The spatial criteria divide algorithms in
terms of their use of velocity, dispersion, and area-of-interest
information. The temporal criteria divide algorithms in terms
of their use of duration information and their local adaptivity.
The taxonomy provides a meaningful labeling and
classification of existing algorithms so that they may be more
easily compared in a systematic way to guide the choice of
algorithms for particular applications.
